pages.title: A modular display
pages.text: Make a Holographic Display Base with its reusable blueprint in a Constructor or Auto Constructor. Place bases side by side at the same level and facing to share a vertical surface.$(br2)Right-click any base to set a common height of 1–10 blocks. Displays need no power or cables.$(br2)Power, Storage, Fluid, Forge Energy and Text modules also have Constructor blueprints. Click or drag a slider; its outer arrows adjust by one.

pages.title: Surface settings
pages.text: Cycle the surface between Invisible, Transparent and Solid. $(thing)Color...$() shows a color preview and opens a hue/shade picker. Choose a shade or press its x to return.$(br2)Transparent mode adds a 0–100% transparency slider: 0% is opaque and 100% fully clear. The default is 87%. Color and transparency are remembered between modes.$(br2)Border is independent and on by default, even on invisible backgrounds. All settings apply to joined bases; older saved presets retain their appearance.

pages.title: Installing modules
pages.text: Right-click a held module to configure it. Sneak-right-click a suitable machine or inventory to link; do this in the air to clear the link.$(br2)Aim at the front of the display. A green rectangle fits; red means overlap or insufficient room. Right-click to install.$(br2)Press and release right-click on an installed module without dragging to edit it, even with empty hands. Sneak-right-click it to recover its configured item. Links and settings stay with recovered modules.

pages.title: Moving modules
pages.text: Hold right-click on an installed module and aim to drag it. You can move across joins between bases on the same screen. The outline is green when it fits and red when it overlaps or leaves the surface.$(br2)Release to place it. An illegal drop snaps back to its original position. Dragging never opens settings on release, even after returning to the starting point. Settings and machine links stay with the module.

pages.title: Power readings
pages.text: Sneak-right-click an Ariente generator, tank, cable or powered machine with a Power module to link it.$(br2)Choose Numbers, Meter or History, and toggle network flux, consumption per tick, generation per tick and fuel remaining. History covers the last 32 seconds of consumption and output.$(br2)Tanks report their generator’s network. Flux is a continuing supply, not a stored battery charge. Unsupported readings show $(thing)n/a$().

pages.title: Storage counts
pages.text: Sneak-right-click an inventory with a Storage module. The clicked side determines which inventory access it reads.$(br2)$(thing)Most stored$() lists up to 16 item types. $(thing)Item grid$() offers 1–64 entries per page, 1–8 columns and a page selector. Larger layouts need more surface space.$(br2)Matching items and tags combine into totals. Readings refresh once per second near players. Unloaded targets stay unloaded and show an offline status; check the link and target if readings stop.

pages.title: Fluid reservoirs
pages.text: Sneak-right-click a tank or machine with a Fluid module. It reads Forge fluid storage exposed on the clicked side, with an unsided fallback. This includes internal machine reservoirs.$(br2)Choose Numbers, Meter or History. Select the first tank (numbered from 1) and show 1–8 consecutive tanks. Empty tanks retain their capacity; a missing tank shows a status.$(br2)Choose millibuckets or buckets, toggle capacity and pick a meter/graph color. Each tank keeps up to 32 observed readings of its contents; changing fluid types starts a new history.

pages.title: Forge Energy
pages.text: Sneak-right-click an FE battery, generator or machine with a Forge Energy module. The clicked side is read first, with an unsided fallback. This module reads Forge Energy storage; use the Power module for Ariente flux.$(br2)Choose Numbers, Meter or History and a meter/graph color. Toggle capacity, percentage and net buffer change per tick; choose abbreviated or exact FE values.$(br2)Net change is the stored-energy difference divided by elapsed game ticks. It combines input and output, so a balanced machine reads zero. The first reading is n/a; history keeps up to 32 observed readings.

pages.title: Camera modules
pages.text: Make a $(item)Camera$() and $(item)Holographic Camera Module$() with their Constructor blueprints. Attach the camera to a floor, wall or ceiling. Its capture origin is two blocks behind its base, including below a floor-mounted camera. It scans connected space around obstacles while keeping sealed caves hidden.$(br2)$(thing)Radius$() sets the capture distance from 8–100 blocks, with a default of 30. $(thing)Zoom$() magnifies that scene from 100–800% without reducing the radius. Sneak-right-click cameras to link, choose Small, Medium or Large, then install the module. Views stay upright on every mounting.

pages.title: Four camera links
pages.text: Sneak-right-click up to four different cameras with the same module. Each new link becomes the selected camera. Relinking an existing camera selects it without adding a duplicate. A fifth camera leaves the four links intact.$(br2)Use $(thing)<$() and $(thing)>$() beside the size selector in the module GUI to select a feed; they wrap around the linked cameras. Installed modules switch immediately. Sneak-right-click in air to clear all links. Only the selected camera is captured.

pages.title: Live camera views
pages.text: View rotation turns the scene around world up; View tilt sets the viewing angle. $(thing)Rotation speed$() ranges from 0–90 degrees per second: 0 stops rotation, and any positive value rotates continuously. New modules start stationary. Animation is smooth between captures. Switch the header selector from $(thing)Orthographic$() to $(thing)Perspective$() for a depth-correct view where nearby objects appear larger. Both modes share the same capture, rotation, tilt and zoom.$(br2)Captures refresh once per second within 32 blocks of a display. Modules using the same camera and radius share a capture. Cameras never load chunks; they work across dimensions when the source is loaded.

pages.title: Reading camera scenes
pages.text: The cyan point marks the camera; cyan markers indicate players and orange markers other living creatures in the scanned space.$(br2)The camera shows surfaces around connected air, including behind pillars and around corners. Sealed caves and buried blocks stay hidden. An open passage or transparent window can expose a cave; closing a door or hatch can hide it again.

pages.title: Camera limits
pages.text: The view uses block models; fluids and blocks with special renderers use simplified silhouettes. An unloaded or removed camera shows its status.$(br2)Scans retain up to 16384 surface blocks. When a large or intricate scene reaches the budget, the outer edge is cropped so terrain inside stays continuous. Internal fluid blocks do not consume the surface budget. Only already loaded terrain is shown.

pages.title: Text and color
pages.text: Left-click the text area to type. Use normal arrow, Home/End, Backspace/Delete, selection and clipboard controls. Escape or clicking outside commits the edit and releases typing.$(br2)Adjust text size, or choose Color... to open a hue/shade picker. Selecting a shade or pressing Back returns to settings. The window’s X closes the whole panel.

pages.title: Alien text
pages.text: Alien Text Modules use sixteen unreadable glyphs. They have no crafting recipe or Constructor blueprint. With ArienteWorld installed, salvage them from displays in city buildings and in floating, huge cube and underground dungeons: sneak-right-click the installed module or break its base.$(br2)Recovered modules work on your own displays and keep their symbols and color. Configure text size and color as usual. Use 0–9 and A–F to select the sixteen symbols; other letters also become alien glyphs. Spaces and line breaks stay blank. These displays are decorative.

pages.title: Changing the layout
pages.text: If an edit makes a module overlap another or outgrow the surface, it is returned with the new settings. A full inventory drops it nearby.$(br2)Shrinking the display is refused if installed modules would be cut off. Move or recover those modules first. Breaking a base returns modules that lose their supporting surface.$(br2)Invisible backgrounds still accept modules and clicks. Power, Storage, Fluid and Forge Energy modules only report readings; they do not transfer resources or control machines.
